_note: Protocol = the paper's R code 1:1 (see the YAML header): measured 2026-08-26 on the refactor/lean-fit branch. Paper Sec. 5.3. Counterfactuals are analytic. The Fig. 6 errors are at x_obs in the SCM's raw units, (2, 1.5, 5.0875, -0.5) = noise (2, 1.5, 1.4, -1) pushed through the SCM; the R code's xObs.csv is that point divided by CAREFL's sample sds (6.0104, 1.9114), (2, 1.5, 0.8465, -0.2616); the paper prints (2, 1.5, 0.81, -0.28), slightly off it. Held-out rows are scored next to it because one point is a noisy yardstick. The R run trained on CAREFL's own X.csv with val = train; this repository draws 2500 rows from the same SCM and a separate 5000-row validation draw. Re-pinned 2026-09-02 at the reference's own 7000 epochs @ lr 0.001 (the CI-runtime compression to 3000 @ 0.002 was reverted after the visual pass against paper Fig. 6: the reference protocol cuts the Fig. 6 curve errors ~30% — x3 2.69->1.87, x4 0.77->0.59 — and every held-out MAE stays within the old bounds; bounds below are 2.5x the new measurement where that is tighter). The residual x4 dip near alpha=0 (~0.3 sd) is a lower-tail quantile artifact at the observed u4 (Laplace tails), partly attributable to the documented raw-units/fresh-draw deviations; the conditional medians are within 0.15 of truth across the grid.

fit_seconds.why: 3x the expected 2-core CI runner wall clock under the reference 7000-epoch protocol (local 151 s ~ CI 250 s est.; re-measure and re-pin from the first CI run): a gross-regression tripwire, not a benchmark
